gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Commanding up top, Righteous fills each line with round bowls and a thin bent-rod stroke. Noto Sans Sundanese is the quiet counterweight, with crossbars that open wide and capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar has curves that leave daylight inside them and short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies, all under Righteous. Make the heading small and its smooth, unmodulated line loses its punch.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Rounded, rope-fine and cheerful, Righteous lays its bent-wire letters across the line with a confident swagger. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri follows with a tall x-height and an a that opens up.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Righteous has no hairlines to squint at, just wide bowls and a firm, bent-rod stroke that holds up anywhere. And Noto Sans Syriac keeps going underneath with blown-glass lowercase bowls and easy, wide-turning s shapes.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-syriac-easter: Fun and forceful, Righteous traces each glyph with a single steady thickness, and its bowls fill the line. Give Noto Sans Syriac Eastern the larger size, since its tall lowercase stands against small caps.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-syriac-wester: Righteous draws bowl-heavy letters with a pen that never shifts pressure or angle, so each line looks bent from rod. And Noto Sans Syriac Western pushes its terminals far from the strokes, giving small letters a dense, bundled-cable body.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Righteous is all full bowls and marker-nib lines that ignore direction. Noto Sans Tagalog sits below with a dense middle zone and generous gaps in its curves, so the text feels open without drifting.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Noto Sans Tagbanwa has open curves with clear gaps and lowercase that fills most of the height, which suits Righteous above it. Noto Sans Tagbanwa stays quiet while the bent-pipe heading, with its constant-width strokes, does the shouting.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Approachable and low-key, Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its ink strokes before they touch and barely steps from capital to lowercase. Righteous is the loud one, a cable bent into shapes; the sans keeps things steady.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Noto Sans Tai Tham reads like chalk-board lowercase crowding toward the capital line, with the inside of each c clearly visible. Righteous brings a fun, commanding shout over it, and the two feel loose and friendly together.
